accepted.s: Which one of the following amendments is correctly matched with its principal subject?
o: 100th Amendment — National Commission for Backward Classes
accepted.x: The 99th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2014, provided for the National Judicial Appointments Commission, which was struck down by the Supreme Court in 2015. The 97th, 100th and 102nd Amendments dealt respectively with co-operative societies, the India-Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement and the constitutional status of the NCBC.
accepted.tq: Use the amendment-subject pair and eliminate swapped subjects from neighbouring amendments.
accepted.sec: Amendment number → subject (97th, 99th, 100th, 101st, 102nd, 103rd, 104th, 105th, 106th)

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The 97th Constitutional Amendment was enacted in 2011.
2. The 100th Constitutional Amendment was enacted in 2015.
3. The 106th Constitutional Amendment was enacted in 2023.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The 97th, 100th and 106th Amendments were enacted in 2011, 2015 and 2023 respectively.
accepted.tq: Match each amendment number with its year before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Amendment number → subject (97th, 99th, 100th, 101st, 102nd, 103rd, 104th, 105th, 106th)

accepted.s: The India-Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement, including exchange of enclaves, was given constitutional effect by the
accepted.x: The 100th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2015, implemented the India-Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement involving the exchange of enclaves.
accepted.tq: Identify the amendment directly associated with the bilateral territorial agreement.
accepted.sec: Amendment number → subject (97th, 99th, 100th, 101st, 102nd, 103rd, 104th, 105th, 106th)

accepted.s: Which of the following is the latest enacted Constitutional Amendment referred to in the current constitutional amendment sequence?
accepted.x: The 106th Constitutional Amendment, enacted in 2023, is the latest enacted amendment in the sequence. The 105th Amendment of 2021 is therefore not the latest.
accepted.tq: Avoid the stale-current-affairs trap by identifying the highest enacted amendment number and year.
accepted.sec: Amendment number → subject (97th, 99th, 100th, 101st, 102nd, 103rd, 104th, 105th, 106th)

accepted.s: Which Article was inserted into the Directive Principles of State Policy by the 97th Constitutional Amendment?
accepted.x: Article 43B was inserted to promote the voluntary formation, autonomous functioning, democratic control and professional management of co-operative societies.
accepted.tq: Use the exact Article number rather than confusing it with the adjacent Article 43A.
accepted.sec: 97th Amendment - co-operatives in Article 19(1)(c), DPSP article, Part IXB

accepted.s: Part IXB of the Constitution, inserted by the 97th Amendment, deals with
accepted.x: Part IXB, comprising Articles 243ZH to 243ZT, contains provisions relating to co-operative societies.
accepted.tq: Match the constitutional Part with its institutional subject.
accepted.sec: 97th Amendment - co-operatives in Article 19(1)(c), DPSP article, Part IXB

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly associated with the constitutional provisions on co-operative societies?
o: Maximum of 21 directors on the board
One seat for an SC or ST member and two seats for women
Audit within six months of the close of the financial year
A six-year fixed term for the board
accepted.x: The board has a five-year term, not a six-year term. The provisions also mention a maximum of 21 directors, one SC/ST seat, two women seats and audit within six months of the close of the financial year.
accepted.tq: Find the single altered numerical or time-limit detail among otherwise correct provisions.
accepted.sec: 97th Amendment - co-operatives in Article 19(1)(c), DPSP article, Part IXB

accepted.s: Elections to the board of a co-operative society under Part IXB are to be held
o: Before the expiry of the board's term
Only after the board's term has expired
At the beginning of every financial year
accepted.x: The election is required to be conducted before the expiry of the board's five-year term.
accepted.tq: Apply the constitutional time-sequence rule to a board whose term is approaching expiry.
accepted.sec: 97th Amendment - co-operatives in Article 19(1)(c), DPSP article, Part IXB

accepted.s: In Rajendra N. Shah v. Union of India (2021), Part IXB was held inapplicable to State co-operative societies mainly because
o: It dealt exclusively with municipal bodies
It had been repealed by the 105th Amendment
It had not been ratified by the States as required
accepted.x: The Supreme Court struck down Part IXB in its application to State co-operative societies because the required ratification by the States had not been obtained. It continues to operate for multi-State co-operative societies.
accepted.tq: Connect the judicial outcome with the precise constitutional procedural defect.
accepted.sec: 97th Amendment - co-operatives in Article 19(1)(c), DPSP article, Part IXB

accepted.s: The Constitution (One Hundred and Twenty-Fourth Amendment) Bill, 2019, which preceded the 103rd Amendment, primarily concerned
accepted.x: The 124th Amendment Bill, 2019, became the 103rd Constitutional Amendment and provided for reservation for economically weaker sections.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the Bill number and the enacted Amendment number.
accepted.sec: 103rd Amendment - EWS reservation extent, bill number, articles amended, Janhit Abhiyan

accepted.s:
With reference to the 103rd Constitutional Amendment, consider the following statements:
1. It enables reservation of up to 10 per cent for EWS.
2. The reservation is outside the existing SC, ST and OBC quotas.
3. The provision makes it mandatory for every State to provide EWS reservation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The EWS reservation is enabling rather than mandatory for the States, so statement 3 is incorrect.
accepted.tq: Watch for the false absolute claim that an enabling constitutional provision is mandatory for every State.
accepted.sec: 103rd Amendment - EWS reservation extent, bill number, articles amended, Janhit Abhiyan

accepted.s: The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam is associated with the
accepted.x: The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam is the 106th Constitutional Amendment Act, receiving assent in 2023.
accepted.tq: Match the popular name of the amendment with its constitutional number and assent year.
accepted.sec: 106th Amendment - Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, assent year, extent, commencement conditions

accepted.s: The Constitution (One Hundred and Twenty-Eighth Amendment) Bill, associated with women's reservation, became the
accepted.x: The 128th Constitutional Amendment Bill became the 106th Constitutional Amendment, popularly known as the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the original Bill number from the final Constitutional Amendment number.
accepted.sec: 106th Amendment - Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, assent year, extent, commencement conditions

accepted.s: The reservation for women under the 106th Constitutional Amendment extends to
o: State Legislative Councils and Rajya Sabha only
The Lok Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies and the Delhi Legislative Assembly
All elected and nominated constitutional bodies
The Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha only
accepted.x: The amendment provides one-third reservation in the Lok Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies and the Delhi Legislative Assembly. It does not extend to the Rajya Sabha or Legislative Councils.
accepted.tq: Compare the expressly covered elected Houses with the Houses excluded from the provision.
accepted.sec: 106th Amendment - Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, assent year, extent, commencement conditions

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding women's reservation under the 106th Constitutional Amendment:
1. It is one-third of the seats in the specified legislative bodies.
2. It includes reservation within seats reserved for SCs and STs.
3. It is initially provided for fifteen years and may be extended.
4. Rotation is linked to delimitation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The amendment provides one-third reservation, including within SC/ST-reserved seats, for an initial period of fifteen years, with possible extension and rotation after each delimitation.
accepted.tq: Check the extent, duration, inclusion and rotation clauses separately before choosing the combined option.
accepted.sec: 106th Amendment - Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, assent year, extent, commencement conditions

accepted.s: The reservation of seats for women under Article 334A is to commence after
o: The expiry of fifteen years from assent
The next Census and the subsequent delimitation exercise
Approval by the Rajya Sabha alone
accepted.x: The reservation is to commence after the next Census and the delimitation conducted thereafter. The relevant Census is referred to as the 2027 Census.
accepted.tq: Identify the conditions precedent rather than treating assent or the next election as sufficient.
accepted.sec: 106th Amendment - Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, assent year, extent, commencement conditions

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the proposed 131st Constitutional Amendment Bill, 2026 is correct?
o: It proposed increasing the Lok Sabha strength from 550 to 850 on the basis of the 2011 Census.
It introduced the GST Council into Article 279A.
It restored the nomination of Anglo-Indians to the Lok Sabha.
It proposed increasing the Rajya Sabha strength from 250 to 550 on the basis of the 2021 Census.
accepted.x: The 131st Amendment Bill, 2026, sought to expand the Lok Sabha from 550 to 850 seats using the 2011 Census as the basis for delimitation.
accepted.tq: Use the paired numerical figures and the stated Census basis to identify the proposal.
accepted.sec: 106th Amendment - Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, assent year, extent, commencement conditions

accepted.s: The 131st Constitutional Amendment Bill, 2026, was
o: referred to the JPC on 17 December 2024
accepted.x: The 131st Amendment Bill, 2026, was defeated on 17 April 2026. The Delimitation Bill, 2026, was withdrawn separately.
accepted.tq: Separate the fate and date of the amendment proposal from the separately withdrawn delimitation Bill.
accepted.sec: 106th Amendment - Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, assent year, extent, commencement conditions

accepted.s: The 104th Constitutional Amendment extended reservation of seats for SCs and STs in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies up to
accepted.x: The 104th Amendment extended SC/ST seat reservation in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies for ten years, up to 2030, under Article 334.
accepted.tq: Calculate neither duration nor date; identify the expressly stated terminal year.
accepted.sec: 104th Amendment - SC/ST seat reservation extension, Anglo-Indian nomination

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the effect of the 104th Constitutional Amendment on Anglo-Indian representation?
o: It increased the number of nominated Anglo-Indian members in both Houses of Parliament.
It transferred the power of nomination from the President to the Election Commission.
It ended the nomination of Anglo-Indian members to the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies.
accepted.x: The 104th Amendment ended the nomination of Anglo-Indian members. Before its discontinuance, the President could nominate two members to the Lok Sabha and the Governor could nominate one member to a State Assembly.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the extension of SC/ST reservation from the simultaneous discontinuance of Anglo-Indian nomination.
accepted.sec: 104th Amendment - SC/ST seat reservation extension, Anglo-Indian nomination

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 331 — One Anglo-Indian member nominated by each Governor
Article 333 — Two Anglo-Indian members nominated by the President to the Lok Sabha
Article 334 — Duration of reservation of seats for SCs and STs
Article 334A — Anglo-Indian nomination in the State Assemblies
accepted.x: Article 334 deals with the duration of reservation of seats for SCs and STs and the related constitutional provisions. Article 331 concerned presidential nomination to the Lok Sabha, Article 333 concerned gubernatorial nomination to State Assemblies, and Article 334A relates to women's reservation.
accepted.tq: Match each Article with its constitutional function and reject exchanged authorities.
accepted.sec: 104th Amendment - SC/ST seat reservation extension, Anglo-Indian nomination

accepted.s: Article 342A, as introduced by the 102nd Constitutional Amendment, initially provided that Socially and Educationally Backward Classes were notified by the
accepted.x: Article 342A provided for the President to notify the Socially and Educationally Backward Classes. The 105th Amendment subsequently restored the States' power to identify SEBCs.
accepted.tq: Keep the constitutional notifier distinct from the Commission that advises on backward classes.
accepted.sec: 102nd and 105th Amendments - NCBC status, who may identify SEBCs, assent

accepted.s: The 105th Constitutional Amendment primarily restored to the States the power to
o: Identify and list Socially and Educationally Backward Classes
accepted.x: The 105th Amendment restored the power of the States to identify and maintain their own lists of Socially and Educationally Backward Classes.
accepted.tq: Focus on the federal distribution of the power to identify SEBCs.
accepted.sec: 102nd and 105th Amendments - NCBC status, who may identify SEBCs, assent

accepted.s: Which expression correctly expands SEBC in the context of Articles 342A and the 105th Amendment?
accepted.x: SEBC means Socially and Educationally Backward Classes. The expression 'Socially and Economically Backward Classes' is not the constitutional expansion used here.
accepted.tq: Test the exact official phrase rather than a familiar but altered expansion.
accepted.sec: 102nd and 105th Amendments - NCBC status, who may identify SEBCs, assent

accepted.s: The Goods and Services Tax was introduced through the 101st Constitutional Amendment, which came into effect on
accepted.x: The 101st Constitutional Amendment was enacted in 2016, and GST was implemented from 1 July 2017.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the year of the amendment from the later date of GST implementation.
accepted.sec: 101st Amendment - GST Council article, articles inserted and omitted

accepted.s: Which Article confers concurrent legislative power on Parliament and State Legislatures to make laws with respect to GST?
accepted.x: Article 246A confers concurrent power on Parliament and State Legislatures to make laws on GST. Article 269A concerns the levy and collection of IGST, while Article 279A deals with the GST Council.
accepted.tq: Separate the three GST Articles by function: legislative power, IGST and the Council.
accepted.sec: 101st Amendment - GST Council article, articles inserted and omitted

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the 101st Constitutional Amendment:
1. Article 246A was inserted.
2. Article 269A was inserted for inter-State GST.
3. Article 279A was inserted for the GST Council.
4. Article 268A was omitted.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The 101st Amendment inserted Articles 246A, 269A and 279A and omitted Article 268A, which related to service tax under the 88th Amendment framework.
accepted.tq: Track both inserted and omitted Articles instead of considering only the newly inserted provisions.
accepted.sec: 101st Amendment - GST Council article, articles inserted and omitted

accepted.s: The GST Council is chaired by the
o: Governor of the Reserve Bank of India
accepted.x: The GST Council constituted under Article 279A is chaired by the Union Finance Minister.
accepted.tq: Apply the 'who would do this job?' method to identify the chairperson of the fiscal federal body.
accepted.sec: 101st Amendment - GST Council article, articles inserted and omitted

accepted.s: Which State was the first to ratify the 101st Constitutional Amendment?
accepted.x: Assam was the first State to ratify the 101st Constitutional Amendment, which required ratification by the States.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive first-ratifier fact rather than confusing it with a major GST-consuming State.
accepted.sec: 101st Amendment - GST Council article, articles inserted and omitted

accepted.s: The Constitution (One Hundred and Twenty-Ninth Amendment) Bill, 2024, primarily concerns
o: The constitutional status of the NCBC
accepted.x: The 129th Amendment Bill, 2024, concerns simultaneous elections under the One Nation, One Election proposal.
accepted.tq: Match the pending Bill number with its stated constitutional subject.
accepted.sec: Constitution amendment bills pending (One Nation One Election, Delhi-related) - subject

accepted.s: Which of the following Articles is proposed to be inserted by the 129th Constitutional Amendment Bill, 2024?
accepted.x: The 129th Amendment Bill proposes insertion of Article 82A and amendments to Articles 83, 172 and 327 in connection with simultaneous elections.
accepted.tq: Identify the newly proposed Article while separating it from Articles inserted by enacted amendments.
accepted.sec: Constitution amendment bills pending (One Nation One Election, Delhi-related) - subject

accepted.s: The 129th Constitutional Amendment Bill, 2024, was introduced on
accepted.x: The 129th Amendment Bill was introduced on 17 December 2024 and was subsequently referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the introduction date from later dates associated with other amendment proposals and committee proceedings.
accepted.sec: Constitution amendment bills pending (One Nation One Election, Delhi-related) - subject

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the 130th Constitutional Amendment Bill, 2025?
o: It provides one-third reservation for women in the Rajya Sabha.
It implements the India-Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement.
It concerns removal of the Prime Minister, Chief Ministers and Ministers detained for 30 consecutive days on serious charges.
It increases the Lok Sabha strength to 850 members.
accepted.x: The 130th Amendment Bill proposes provisions concerning the removal of the Prime Minister, Chief Ministers and Ministers detained for 30 consecutive days on serious charges. It also involves Articles 75, 164 and 239AA, including Delhi.
accepted.tq: Identify the Bill by its distinctive consequence and detention-duration condition.
accepted.sec: Constitution amendment bills pending (One Nation One Election, Delhi-related) - subject

accepted.s: The 130th Constitutional Amendment Bill, 2025, proposes amendments to which group of Articles?
accepted.x: The 130th Bill proposes amendments to Articles 75, 164 and 239AA, relating respectively to the Union Council of Ministers, State Councils of Ministers and the special provisions for Delhi.
accepted.tq: Match the pending Bill with its Article cluster rather than with the subject of another amendment.
accepted.sec: Constitution amendment bills pending (One Nation One Election, Delhi-related) - subject

accepted.s:
Arrange the following Constitutional Amendments in chronological order of enactment:
A. 103rd Amendment
B. 101st Amendment
C. 105th Amendment
D. 102nd Amendment
accepted.x: The 101st Amendment was enacted in 2016, the 102nd in 2018, the 103rd in 2019 and the 105th in 2021. Therefore, the correct order is B, D, A, C.
accepted.tq: Place the amendments by year first, then compare only the closely spaced entries.
accepted.sec: Amendment number → subject (97th, 99th, 100th, 101st, 102nd, 103rd, 104th, 105th, 106th)
